min_stable_gain.value: set by C_C: unity-gain stable with C_C = 10 pF; C_C = 0 pF recommended only for noise gain >= 10
min_stable_gain.conditions: Figure 59 (suggested C_C vs noise gain for 1 dB peaking) and Table 6
min_stable_gain.below_minimum: Data sheet states the compensation capacitor depends on the circuit noise gain, not the voltage gain (noninverting G_N = R_F/R_G + 1, inverting G_N = R_F/R_G + 1). Reducing C_C raises bandwidth and peaking (lower phase margin); increasing C_C lowers bandwidth and raises phase margin. A capacitor C_F across R_F compensates the phase loss from feedback resistance and input capacitance (Fig. 14: R_F = 1 kOhm with C_F = 2.2 pF). No TIA-specific guidance.

pinout_notes: 1 LOGIC REFERENCE, 2 -IN, 3 +IN, 4 -V_S, 5 C_COMP (C_C to -V_S), 6 V_OUT, 7 +V_S, 8 DISABLE (active low). Enabled when pin 8 is ~2 V or more above pin 1; disabled within ~1.5 V; both open = enabled. Disabled: 1.3 mA, off isolation -40 dB at 10 MHz, t_on 45 ns, t_off 50 ns (PDF 9 / p8, PDF 4 / p3).

tia_content.what: No TIA example or equations. Relevant: compensation depends on noise gain (Table 6, Fig. 59); C_F across R_F to offset the pole from feedback resistance and input capacitance (text and Fig. 14: R_F = 1 kOhm, C_F = 2.2 pF in a G = +2 circuit)

application_guidance: Layout (PDF 22 / p21, Fig. 62): guard ring around pin 5 tied to the output pin 6 (same potential) to shield the high-impedance compensation node and cut stray capacitance; C_C as a COG/NPO surface-mount part adjacent to the package between pins 4 and 5 (no leaded capacitors); bypass capacitors right at pins 4 and 7; R_F beneath the board from pin 6 to pin 2; R_G return next to the pin-4 bypass. Capacitive loads: raise C_C or add R_SNUB (Fig. 71: ~17.5 Ohm for C_L >= 25 pF at G = +2 for 2 dB peaking). Source resistance forms a pole with the input capacitance (Fig. 15). Larger resistors raise noise; smaller R_F raises distortion (Fig. 22, 25).
abs_max_and_input_protection: Supply 26.4 V; common-mode input +/-V_S +/-1 V; differential input +/-0.8 V; differential input current +/-10 mA (input diodes, no series current-limiting resistors to keep noise low; limit current to 10 mA if differential input exceeds 0.8 V); output short-circuit duration per derating curves; operating -40 to +85 C; storage -65 to +125 C; T_J 150 C (175 C extended -> failure) (PDF 8 / p7).
other_notes: Fig. 37 voltage-noise trace sits at 2.35-2.4 nV/rtHz in the flat region although annotated '2.1nV/rtHz' (table TYP 2.1, MAX 2.6).
Fig. 58 simplified diagram text gives ~200 MHz at G = +1 with C_C = 10 pF, versus 490 MHz TYP in Table 1 (instructional figure).
Features list '200 MHz (G = -1), 190 MHz (G = -10)' and 'constant bandwidth from G = -1 to G = -10' refer to inverting gains with adjusted C_C.
No differential input capacitance specified; common-mode 1 pF only.
Bias current 7.5 uA TYP flows in the inputs (NPN pair).
